body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-N26-PH-DISPATCH-EVENTS-PARSER` (pool: codex-personal), single commit on base `a6f3c3233`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-N26-PH-DISPATCH-EVENTS-PARSER

Implemented a typed dispatch event parser in src/core/fabric/dispatch-events.ts
and a read-only `phm fleet events` command. Supports RESTOCK, LAUNCH_FAILED,
LANE_HOLD and the PUBLISH_* family; keeps payloads as uninterpreted text.
The reader streams records, filters inclusively by timestamp instant, retains
file order and reports malformed/blank lines and missing logs separately.
The CLI supports --since, --file and --json, rejects unknown/repeated arguments,
and reports read errors without echoing file contents. Operator usage is in
docs/HUB-REFERENCE.md. No dependencies or credentials were added.

Compatibility limitation: this checkout and the available historical bridge
snapshot contain no dispatch-events.log writer or format contract. The parser
accepts an ISO timestamp with an explicit timezone, optionally bracketed,
followed by whitespace, the event kind and optional payload. Fixtures document
that grammar. The default location is ~/.ashlr/fabric/dispatch-events.log;
--file supports externally managed router logs. A sanitized production example
or the actual writer is still needed to verify live router compatibility.
No adjacent dead code was found to remove.

Validation commands and results:

- HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/dispatch-events.test.ts: passed twice,
  1 file and 28 tests per run, 0 failures. Covers every event kind, malformed

All changes are uncommitted. No commit, push, tag, publish.sh or PR creation

No .github files, CODEOWNERS, release/publish configuration or Tier-1 paths
were edited. No secrets or tokens were accessed or printed.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-RECUTQUEUE63
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-RECUTQUEUE63` (pool: claude), single commit on base `da181be3b`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-RECUTQUEUE63

Recut of #1166 (bridge: RQ-N26-PH-DISPATCH-EVENTS-PARSER, opened 2026-10-26).

Closes #1166

## What landed

A typed, read-only parser for the dispatcher's text log `dispatch-events.log`,
exposed as `phm fleet dispatch-events [--since <ISO>] [--file <path>] [--json]`.

Why it was still missing: master's `phm fleet events` (src/core/fleet/events.ts)
replays **JSON** rows only. dispatchd/restock write plain text rows
(`%F %T KIND payload`, contrib/mac/dispatchd.py `ev()`), so `fleet events` skips
every one of them. No other shared parser exists. About 15 CLI files each use
their own ad-hoc regex.

Adaptations from the original PR, with reasons:
- **Verb renamed** `fleet events` → `fleet dispatch-events`. Master already
  ships `fleet events` with a different meaning (JSON queue event stream).
- **No `src/cli/fleet.ts` edit** (it's a forbidden path). The verb is the
  convention file `src/cli/fleet-dispatch-events.ts` exporting
  `cmdFleetDispatchEvents`, plus one line in `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`.
  I re-checked that line against a fresh `origin/master`: the registry is unchanged there.
- **Real log format accepted.** The PR's notes said it had no writer to check
  against and only parsed ISO-with-timezone rows. The recut also parses
  dispatchd's local `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` rows and accepts any uppercase kind.
  The original only allowed RESTOCK/LAUNCH_FAILED/LANE_HOLD/PUBLISH_*, but
  dispatchd emits about 40 kinds. Each event gains `at` (the same instant in UTC ISO).
- **Real default path.** The PR used `~/.ashlr/fabric/dispatch-events.log`,
  which nothing writes. The recut uses the canonical candidates from
  `core/fleet/dispatch-events-path.ts`: `~/.ashlr-runs/queue/dispatch-events.log`,
  then `~/.ashlr-runs/dispatch-events.log`.
- **Bounded.** At most the newest 5000 matches are kept, and the overflow is
  reported as `truncated`. Memory is bounded while streaming, so a long-lived
  log can't grow the result without limit.
- Dropped: the PR's `fleet.ts` switch case and help line (forbidden path), and
  the docs code-block line. `doc-facts` requires every documented verb to be in
  completions `SUBCOMMANDS`, and `src/cli/completions.ts` is touched by the
  parallel RECUTBUSGRAPH61 and RECUTNONPHXNEW62 worktrees. The prose doc in
  `docs/HUB-REFERENCE.md` was kept. Follow-up: add `dispatch-events` to the
  completions fleet list once those land.

No admission, disk-guard or memory-pressure check is touched. The command only reads.

## Candidates checked (oldest first, open-PR snapshot of 2026-11-09 23:08)

`gh` wasn't authenticated in this worker, and the unauthenticated GitHub API was
rate-limited. I used the open-PR list another worker saved at 23:08 (326 PRs)
and fetched every PR head over git.
- #915 custody/receipt hold: needs `src/core/daemon/loop.ts` (CODEOWNERS) and its subject is secrets custody. Skipped.
- #927 local-vs-frontier routing eval: the core is `src/core/routing/policy.ts` and `tiers.ts`, and `/src/core/routing/**` is in CODEOWNERS. It's also about 1200 lines. Skipped (still missing from master).
- #935, #948, #976 (coding CLI adapters, router mega-PRs): `src/core/routing/**` is in CODEOWNERS, and they span 20 to 80 files. Skipped.
- #950: being recut by RQ-PHX-RECUTVERSEA61.
- #1048: its queue CLI/journal/stats are on master already; the remaining queue-stats UI overlaps RECUTVERSEA61.
- #1149: an 11k-line refactor of `fleet/status.ts`, not a behavior change. Skipped.
- **#1166: genuinely missing. Recut here.**

## Size

`git diff --stat origin/master` plus untracked: **6 files** (the PR had 6), about 387 lines:
- src/core/fabric/dispatch-events.ts (new, 151)
- src/cli/fleet-dispatch-events.ts (new, 50)
- src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts (+1)
- docs/HUB-REFERENCE.md (+11)
- test/recut-queue-1166.test.ts (new, 162)
- test/fixtures/dispatch-events/events.txt (new, 12)

## Commands run (HOME=$(mktemp -d))

- `npx vitest run test/recut-queue-1166.test.ts`: 35/35 passed
- `npx vitest run test/fleet-registry-help.test.ts`: 375/375
- `npx vitest run test/fleet-subcommand-registry.test.ts`: 387/387
- `npx vitest run test/fleet-verb-help-smoke.test.ts`: 376/376
- `npx vitest run test/fleet-verb-convention.test.ts`: 16/16; `fleet-verb-export-convention`: 1/1; `fleet-verb-catalog`: 4/4
- `npx vitest run test/docs-fleet-verbs.test.ts`: 30/30; `cli-completions-subcommands`: 12/12
- `npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts`: 6/6 (it failed once on the docs code line, which I then removed)
- `npm run check:docs`: errors []
- eslint on the 4 changed TS files: clean. The worktree's `node_modules/eslint/lib`
  is missing (incomplete install), so I ran a complete eslint 9.39.5 from another
  worktree against a scratch copy of this tree with the repo's `eslint.config.js`.
- Typecheck:
  `tsgo` is not installed here (npx 404), so I used the fallback
  `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json --incremental false`: **exit 0**.

Nothing is committed; all changes are left uncommitted in the worktree.
</details>

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-RECUTDESKNEW68` (pool: claude), single commit on base `155ebde0f`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-RECUTDESKNEW68: recut of #4555 (RQ-PHX-DISKRUNWAYHOST52)

Supersedes #4555

**Chosen PR:** #4555, "bridge: RQ-PHX-DISKRUNWAYHOST52" (mergeable_state `unstable`: Merge Gate and Quick typecheck red).

**What Mason sees:** a "Disk runway" card on the desktop Host pane, under Memory guard, refreshed every 30 s:
`Disk: 283 GB free`, `~7.0 h until new jobs are held`, the sample window and GB/h, and the two lines
(100 GB reuse-only, 30 GB no launches). Below 100 GB the card turns red with "new jobs are held (reuse-only)".
Below 30 GB it turns a stronger red with "no launches". When there is no reading it shows "free space unknown"
and never invents a number. The route is read-only and has no repair or dispatch authority.

## Candidate selection (newest first, number >= 4300, touches `src/web-ui/routes/verse/**`)
`gh` could not read its config in this sandbox, so I used the public REST API plus `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head`,
and computed file lists with `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base origin/master pr) pr`.
- #4590 (RQ-PHX-RECUTTOPA59): skipped. It edits `test/verse-workbench-contracts-310.test.ts`, which is listed in origin/master:.github/CODEOWNERS.
- #4567 (RQ-PHX-MERGEWAITCARD54): skipped. #4590's body says "Supersedes #4567".
- #4555 (RQ-PHX-DISKRUNWAYHOST52): **chosen**. No CODEOWNERS, `.github/**`, desktop-core or src-tauri paths. No other PR says "Supersedes #4555".
  Content check: none of its 5 added files exist on origin/master (`git cat-file -e`), and
  `git grep` finds none of `DiskRunwayCard`, `fleet-disk-runway-api`, `diskRunway` or `disk-runway-query` on origin/master.

## Why #4555 was red, and the fix
The PR mounted its handler by adding `fleet-disk-runway` to `DEFAULT_API_MODULES` in `src/core/verse/verse-api.ts`.
The frozen A10 mount table is pinned entry by entry in `test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts`, a CODEOWNERS (Tier-1) file.
With that entry, 3 tests in that suite failed (reproduced locally). This recut must not touch that file.

So the recut serves the route through the fleet-control workbench family, the same way recently landed #4581 serves
`/api/verse/fleet/control/launch-stall`:
- `VERSE_FLEET_DISK_RUNWAY_PATH` is now `/api/verse/fleet/control/disk-runway` (it was `/api/verse/fleet/disk-runway`).
- `src/core/verse/fleet-control-api.ts` lazily dispatches that exact path to `handleFleetDiskRunwayApi`. This is 4 lines, re-applied by hand.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/disk-runway-query.ts` fetches the new path.
- `src/core/verse/verse-api.ts` is left at master's version: no mount-table edit.
Non-GET requests on the fleet-control prefix still go through the V1 mutation gate before the handler's 405.

## Named paths (`git checkout pr-4555 -- <path>`)
- src/core/verse/fleet-disk-runway-api.ts (path constant and header comment edited)
- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/DiskRunwayCard.tsx
- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/DiskRunwayCard.test.tsx
- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/disk-runway-query.ts (route path edited)
- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/FleetHostPane.tsx
- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/fleet-host.module.css
- test/fleet-disk-runway-api.test.ts
- src/core/verse/verse-api.ts: checked out, then reverted to origin/master (see above). It is replaced by a hand edit to src/core/verse/fleet-control-api.ts.

New: `test/recut68-desk-new.test.ts`. It drives the real `handleFleetControlApi` with the default (uninjected) reader
against a temp `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR`. Disk-growth samples of 283 -> 263 GB over 2 h give 10 GB/h, 16.3 h to reuse-only and 23.3 h to hard stop.
With no ledgers it reports unknown/null and makes up no runway.

## Diff
`git diff --stat origin/master`: 8 PR files (262 insertions), plus BRIDGE_NOTES.md and test/recut68-desk-new.test.ts = 10 files.
Net LOC: +326 code/test lines (262 + 64), 0 deletions, plus these notes.

## Commands and results
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/recut68-desk-new.test.ts test/fleet-disk-runway-api.test.ts test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts`: 3 files, 40/40 passed. The mount suite failed 3 tests with the PR's original mount entry.

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-host/`: 22 files, 121/121 passed (includes DiskRunwayCard.test.tsx).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json --incremental false`: exit 0.
- `npx eslint <8 changed files + new test>`: exit 0. The worktree's `node_modules/eslint` was missing `lib/` (the main checkout's copy is broken the same way).
  I restored it locally from a scratch install of the same version, eslint@9.39.5. It is not part of the diff.

  #4588 (RECUTTOPC59), about #3514. Neither PR supersedes or carries them, so no
  other recut owns them. I treated a passing mention as not ownership.

## Audit list (oldest first, 1 of at most 6 audited)

- **#4259 RQ-PHX-RECONCILEDECLINE09STM1**: real missing work, so it is recovered
  here. Its own commit is 89182a4449; the other 25 commits on the branch are
  `Merge branch 'master'`. Its own paths:

  - `src/core/cos/decline.ts` (A): missing on master. `git grep declineCos` on
    origin/master finds nothing.
  - `src/core/cos/intake.ts` (M): master's `cosStatus` has no `declined` state.
  - `test/cos-decline-preservation-09stm1.test.ts` (A): ported into the new
    recut test.

The rule is to stop at the first PR with missing work, so I did not audit
#4262, #4275, #4280 or #4286. Their own commits for the next recut are
7fa97fe121, 1a6b9f5824, f886dd8f02 and 19d3156bd3.

## What was carried and how

- `src/core/cos/decline.ts`: new file. It keeps the PR's behavior and error
  text. The decline binds the displayed draft digest and takes the same
  exclusive `wx` delivery claim as an approved send, so exactly one of decline
  and send wins. A `sending`, `sent` or `uncertain` claim is never overwritten
  (EEXIST). Then it closes the needs-you item on a best-effort basis.
- `src/cli/fleet-cos-decline.ts`: taken verbatim from 89182a4449 (convention
  dispatch, `cmdFleetCosDecline`).
- `src/core/cos/intake.ts`: the PR's hunk is ported by hand: the `declined`
  state, and `needsYou` is false once a draft is declined. The PR copied the
  digest-binding check and the needs-you cleanup from `deliverCosResult`.
  Instead, both now live in shared exports (`boundCosDraft`, `cosDeliveryPath`,
  `closeCosNeedsYou`), so approval and decline enforce one binding. I also added
  `export type CosDelivery`. The binding now also requires a 64-hex digest.
  That is strictly tighter: stored digests are always sha256 hex, and the API
  passes the stored digest.
- `src/core/cos/list.ts`: **not in the PR.** The PR widened `cosStatus`'s
  delivery type, but `CosTaskSummary.delivery` stayed at the old union, which
  leaves the types mismatched. It now uses `CosDelivery`.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`: **not in the PR.** The file is
  generated by `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`, which added one line.
  Without it, `phm fleet cos-decline` could not be reached.
- `docs/COS.md`: documents the verb, next to "There is no CLI approval command."
- `test/cos-decline-recutolde60.test.ts`: new. It covers:
  - the PR's five cases: digest binding, races, keeping sending/sent/uncertain,
    concurrent claim, CLI validation;
  - dispatch through `cmdFleet(['cos-decline', …])` and the registry loader;
  - `listCosTasks` reporting `declined` with `needsYou: false`;
  - reconcile refusing a declined claim;
  - unknown, invalid and draft-less ids.

The desktop and API approve path (`fleet-cos-api.ts`) already answers
`COS_ALREADY_CLAIMED` for any existing claim, so it refuses a declined draft
without changes.

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PHX-RECUTOLDA60

## Summary

Recovered the oldest stranded RQ-PHX PR in range 2600-2999 whose work was not on
master: **#2774 (RQ-PHX-SAFARIIMPORTVERB01)**, the TypeScript driver for
`scripts/mac-bridge/safari_import.py` (`ashlr fleet safari-import <status|begin-import>`).

After #2774 was opened, master reused the verb name `safari-import` for a different
NEEDS-MASON ask flow (#3292, RQ-PHX-SAFARIIMPORTASK03:
`[--json] [--apply | --done] [--runs-dir]`). `safari_import.py` is on master,
byte-identical to the PR's copy, but no TypeScript code invoked it. The recut keeps the
ask flow unchanged and adds the PR's helper modes as positional subcommands of the same
verb:

- `ashlr fleet safari-import` with no mode word runs the existing ask flow, unchanged.
- `ashlr fleet safari-import status|begin-import [--root] [--timeout 1-120] [--json]`
  runs `python3 -I safari_import.py <mode> --needs-mason <abs> --timeout N` via execFile
  (never a shell), with a kill bound of timeout + 15s. Exit codes propagate (2 = blocked
  on a human step), child stderr is never echoed, and import/sign-in success is claimed
  only when the helper asserts it.
- A bare word anywhere in argv (skipping the values of `--runs-dir`/`--root`/`--timeout`)
  routes to the helper path, which validates the mode against a closed list before
  anything spawns.
- `--help`/`-h` anywhere prints the combined usage and exits 0. This matches the CLAUDE.md
  convention; previously only a lone `--help` was accepted.

The bridge logic lives in `src/core/fleet/safari-import-helper.ts`, per the thin-CLI rule
(the PR had put it in `src/cli/`). The ported logic is otherwise unchanged from #2774.

title: bridge: RQ-MERGEBLOCKERSQ8
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-MERGEBLOCKERSQ8` (pool: devin), single commit on base `933b95223`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/fleet-merge-age.test.ts test/fleet-merge-queue-age.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-MERGEBLOCKERSQ8

Job: extend the existing merge queue observer (`phm fleet merge-queue-age` /
`mergeQueueAge`, continuing the RQ-MERGEAGEQ8 → RQ-MERGEQUEUEAGEQ8 series) to
classify pending required checks, conflicts, and stale branches with
timestamps, and to enqueue an idempotent recut for conflicts through the
existing merge-queue recut path.

## What changed

### `src/core/fleet/merge-age.ts` — blocker classification with timestamps

- New optional snapshot evidence: `prs[].mergeStateStatus`, `updatedAt`,
  `headSha`, `repo`, `recutRequests`, `lastRecutHead`; `queue[].requiredChecks[].at`;
  input-level `repo`. All additive; old snapshots still validate.
- Every `cause` now carries `since`: per-check `at` (falling back to the queue
  entry's `enteredAt`) for `check_pending` / `check_failure` / `check_missing`,
  and the PR's `updatedAt` for `conflicts`, `stale` and `review`. Unparseable
  or future timestamps stay `null` — unknown, never guessed.
- New `stale` cause for `mergeStateStatus` `BEHIND` (case-insensitive); `DIRTY`
  now counts as a conflict alongside `mergeable: CONFLICTING` (the same
  convention `merge-batch` uses). A present `mergeStateStatus` also satisfies
  the `mergeability` missing-data flag when `mergeable` is absent/UNKNOWN.

### `src/core/fleet/merge-queue-age.ts` — automatic idempotent recut enqueue

- Each conflicting active queue entry now produces one recut enqueue row in
  `retryable_conflicts` — `{number, repo, head_sha, waiting_s, since, recut}`
  where `recut` is the shared `MergeRecutRequest` from `merge-eta.ts`
  (`RQ-RECUT-<repo>-<pr>-<sha7>`). This is the same idempotency token the
  existing merge-queue recut path (recut loop, `phm fleet merge-recover`,
  `queue-latency`, `merge-latency`) already dedupes on, so a repeat
  observation of the same head never enqueues a second recut and a moved
  head mints a new key.
- `blocked_conflicts` reports the honest reason nothing was enqueued:
  `ambiguous` (duplicate queue or PR rows, reported once per PR), `no-repo`,
  `no-head`, `already-requested` (`lastRecutHead` covers this head), or
  `too-many-recuts` (≥ `MAX_QUEUE_AGE_RECUTS = 3` recorded `recutRequests`) —
  the same bounds `queue-latency` and `merge-latency` apply.
- Report stays `fleet.merge-queue-age.v1`, `readOnly: true`,
  `requiredChecksPreserved: true`; merged/closed PRs are still excluded and
  required checks pass through per-entry unmodified.
- `phm fleet merge-recover` embeds this report in its `queue` field, so its
  JSON now carries `retryable_conflicts` / `blocked_conflicts` for free.

### `src/cli/fleet-merge-age.ts` / `fleet-merge-queue-age.ts`

- `validMergeAgeInput` validates the new optional fields (bounded strings,
  repo slug `owner/name`, non-negative `recutRequests`); both commands and
  `merge-recover` share it.
- `merge-queue-age` usage documents the new fields and plain output prints
  `Conflicts the recut loop can retry: #N (RQ-RECUT-…)` plus one
  `Needs a person: #N (reason)` per blocked conflict — mirroring
  `merge-latency`'s phrasing.

### Docs

- `docs/FLEET-API.md` merge-queue-age section describes `since` timestamps,
  stale-branch classification and the keyed recut enqueue/dedup contract.

## Acceptance mapping

- **Classify pending required checks, conflicts, stale branches with
  timestamps**: `check_pending`/`check_failure`/`check_missing` carry
  `check.at` else `enteredAt`; `conflicts` (CONFLICTING or DIRTY) and `stale`
  (BEHIND) carry `updatedAt`. Covered by new fixtures.
- **Automatically enqueue an idempotent recut for conflicts through the
  existing merge queue path**: `retryable_conflicts` emits one keyed
  `RQ-RECUT-` request per conflicting head — the token the existing recut
  path enqueues exactly once.
- **Fixtures prove no duplicate recuts**: re-observing the same head mints
  the identical key; `lastRecutHead` → `already-requested`,
  `recutRequests ≥ 3` → `too-many-recuts`, duplicate rows → one `ambiguous`
  block, merged/closed → nothing.
- **Preserve required checks**: `requiredChecksPreserved: true`, per-entry
  `requiredChecks` pass through unmodified, and the input snapshot is never
  mutated (asserted via `structuredClone`).

## Commands run

- `npm run install:worktree` — pnpm store install, ok
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-merge-queue-age.test.ts
  test/fleet-merge-age.test.ts` — 11/11 passed
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-merge-recover.test.ts
  test/doc-facts.test.ts` — 14/14 passed
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run` on all three touched suites together —
  19/19 passed
- `npm run typecheck:fast` (tsgo, backend + web) — exit 0
- `npx eslint` on all six touched ts files — exit 0
- `npm run check:docs` — 0 errors
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — all PASS
  (file selection, fleet registry, authority drift, eslint, tsgo,
  realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe)
- `npm run dev -- fleet merge-queue-age --input <fixture>` — end-to-end
  plain output verified (stale + conflict causes, retry line, needs-person)

## Pass/fail counts

- Touched tests: 19/19 pass (11 merge-queue-age incl. 5 new/extended cases,
  6 merge-age incl. 1 new case, 3 merge-recover, 14 doc-facts total run).
- verify-changed: all PASS.

## Net LOC

- `git diff --shortstat`: 7 files changed, +283 / −27, net +256.
- BRIDGE_NOTES.md is untracked and not counted.

## Limits

- The observer stays read-only per its schema contract: it emits the
  idempotent recut request the existing path enqueues; it does not itself
  write drop jobs (that remains the recut loop / `merge-recover --apply`,
  which needs path evidence a queue snapshot does not carry).
- `since` reflects the best snapshot evidence; a snapshot without
  `updatedAt`/`check.at` reports `null` rather than a guessed time.
</details>

# RQ-PHX-NEEDSYOUHARDLIMIT55: hard-limit chips in the Needs-you drawer

Serves t1637u. On origin/master (44eada4c02, fast-forwarded to 933b952237) the
drawer did not call `classifyNeedsItem`. Only FleetNeedsYouRows' "Needs Mason"
group used it, through needs-mason-triage-model.ts. So this change was needed.

## What changed
- NEW `src/web-ui/routes/verse/shell/needs-you-hard-limit.ts`: a pure model.
  - `hardLimitLabel(text)` is built on core `classifyNeedsItem` (value import).
    It maps: secrets → "Only you: secrets", money → "Only you: money",
    outside-send → "Only you: outside send", destroy-data → "Only you: deletes
    data". Everything else → "Phantom can clear".
  - `splitByHardLimit(items)` returns `{ onlyYou, phantom, counts }` in input
    order, keyed on `item.title`.
- `NeedsYouList.tsx`: new optional `limits` prop. Each row shows the label as a
  `.chip` next to the existing triage chip.
- `NeedsYouDrawer.tsx`: computes labels from each item's title. A new
  "Asks" toolbar (reuses `.batch`/`.batchCount`) shows "N of M need only you"
  and the toggle button "Only my asks (N)" (`aria-pressed`). Plain `useState`;
  nothing is persisted. J/K, picks and the batch bar all act on the filtered
  list.
- No CSS change. The chip reuses existing tones: `held` (amber) for only-you,
  `clean` (green) for Phantom can clear. This kept the diff to 5 files.
- `needs-mason-triage.ts` patterns are unchanged. No auto-resolve action.

## Decisions to review
- `authority` (signing, notarize, standing approvals, grants) is labelled
  "Only you: signing or grants", not "Phantom can clear". Release trust is
  reserved for the owner, so the chip must not call it clearable.
- `unrecognized` is labelled "Phantom can clear". The spec requires this (the
  "tokenizer" case). Core's auto-resolve still treats unrecognized text as
  needs-Mason. That is unaffected, because the chip is a label only.
- Only the title is classified, not the detail. Words like "text" or "reply"
  in body prose would otherwise flag ordinary PR rows.
- If the filter is on and no hard-limit rows remain, the filter lapses and the
  full list shows. An empty filtered list must never render "All clear" while
  other rows still wait. The button is disabled at N = 0.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-MERGELATENCYN9Q8

Bounded automatic retry for transient merge-queue failures, built on the
existing merge-event ledger and ordinary GitHub auto-merge.

## Summary

The merge-queue coordinator is `phm fleet merge-latency`
(`src/cli/fleet-merge-latency.ts`): a JSONL event ledger
(`recordMergeEvent`/`readMergeEvents`) plus a report computing
opened→queued, queued→merged and total durations, per-PR stage timings,
blocker reasons, pending auto-merge stalls and retryable conflicts.
`phm fleet merge-recover` (`src/cli/fleet-merge-recover.ts`) already owns
the safe re-arm path: `gh pr merge --auto --match-head-commit <sha>`.

Changes:

- `src/cli/fleet-merge-latency.ts` — new `retry_requested` event type
  (recordable via `--record`), `MAX_QUEUE_RETRIES = 3`, and a
  `queue_retries` report section. `queueRetryVerdict()` classifies an open
  PR whose latest timed toggle is `auto_merge_disabled` after a timed
  `auto_merge_enabled`: `retryable` only when the newest recorded blocker
  in that episode is `queue` and retries remain; `needs_person` rows carry
  `unattributed` (no queue blocker, or an untimed toggle leaves armed
  state unknown), `already-requested` (a retry at/after the disable) or
  `too-many-retries` (3 distinct requests). Replayed identical
  `retry_requested` lines dedupe by `at|head_sha`. Report stays
  read-only — never merge authority.
- `src/cli/fleet-merge-retry.ts` (new) — `phm fleet merge-retry
  [--events f] [--apply] [--json]`. Dry run by default; `--apply`
  re-reads each candidate live (`pr view`), skips armed/draft/conflict/
  finished/held PRs, and re-arms with `gh pr merge --auto
  --match-head-commit` — the same head-pinned call merge-recover uses.
  One `retry_requested` event is appended per successful request, so a
  second run is a no-op (`already-requested`). Bounds: 3 retries per PR
  ever, `MAX_REQUESTS_PER_RUN = 3` requests per run. Exit 1 on
  unreadable ledger or a failed request (a failed request consumes no
  retry).
- `src/cli/fleet-merge-recover.ts` — exported the existing hold set as
  `PHANTOM_PR_HOLDS` so merge-retry honours the same holds.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` — regenerated (`merge-retry`).
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` — regenerated; new Tier-1 root:
  `/test/fleet-merge-retry.test.ts @masonwyatt23`.
- `docs/FLEET-MERGE-LATENCY.md`, `docs/FLEET-API.md`, `docs/README.md` —
  documented the event, the report fields, the command and the safety
  model.
- `test/fleet-merge-latency.test.ts` — classification coverage
  (retryable ordering, `unattributed`, `already-requested`,
  `too-many-retries`, non-queue blockers invisible, merged/closed/
  re-armed PRs excluded, untimed toggle → `unattributed`).
- `test/fleet-merge-retry.test.ts` (new) — success, retry exhaustion,
  duplicate/replayed events, per-run cap, holds, live-state skips,
  provider failure, arg validation, registry reachability.

Safety: required checks, reviews and the merge queue stay in force — the
retry only re-arms ordinary head-pinned auto-merge; GitHub merges when
checks pass on their own. No `--admin`, no bypass flags, no unpinned
heads, no workflow/permissions changes.

## Recorded findings (fixture ledger exercised end-to-end)

No real `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/merge-events.jsonl` exists on this
machine; a fixture with 2 merged PRs, pending auto-merges, blocker
observations and two dropped auto-merges was run through the built CLI:

- Merged: 2 — opened→queued median 300 s, queued→merged median 1800 s,
  total median 2100 s; slowest step `queue_to_merge`.
- Stalled reasons: `#13` retryable dropped auto-merge (3 retries left);
  `#14` `needs-person (unattributed)` — disable with no queue blocker.
- `merge-retry` dry run: `#13 → request-auto-merge`,
  `#14 → needs-person (unattributed)`; zero `gh` calls in dry run.

## Commands run

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs` | registry regenerated (`merge-retry`) |
| `npm run authority:regen` | CODEOWNERS regenerated (1 new Tier-1 root) |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-merge-latency.test.ts test/fleet-merge-retry.test.ts test/fleet-merge-recover.test.ts` | 3 files / 36 tests pass |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts test/fleet-registry-help.test.ts` | 2 files / 378 tests pass |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx tsgo --noEmit` | pass, 0 errors |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) ./node_modules/.bin/eslint <5 touched files>` | pass, clean |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs --force` | all PASS: file selection, fleet registry, authority drift (10 authority tests), eslint changed files, tsgo, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` | pass, `errors: []` |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run build` | `tsc` + vite pass; `build-release-dependency-inventory` fails with ENOENT lstat `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.9.0/lib/node_modules` — pre-existing host keg-layout quirk, unrelated to this diff |

authority tests inside verify-changed; zero failures. Full build
orchestration partially blocked by the environmental issue noted.

# RQ-TRAIN-MASTER-NEXT-1

## Change / proposed PR description

A release tag accepted through its release-please ancestor could remain behind
master indefinitely: the build correctly refused to build master as that old
version, but the train never requested a successor release PR. Once hourly
cadence is due and master has commits after that tag, the planner now records
`advance.action=advance-from-master`, the next patch and observed master SHA,
with reason `candidate-not-master-head -> plan <version>` and next step

If the expected release PR exists, the train waits for its checks and uses the
existing merge queue enqueue path. Otherwise it dispatches the existing
`release-please.yml` workflow on master with no inputs. That workflow independently
checks green master, cadence and version carriers. Existing tag collision refusal
remains in place. Tags are never moved/deleted; signing, notarization, attestation,
secret gates, permissions and merge queue checks are unchanged. No live Mac files
were installed or edited.

Mac wrapper. It blocks desktop completion, but does not block npm dispatch when
build, attestation and audit evidence are available. It is an external publisher
handoff, not a train policy hold to remove. `phantom-secrets` identifies the

title: bridge: RQ-PHANTOM-VERSE-CPU-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHANTOM-VERSE-CPU-1` (pool: claude), single commit on base `933b95223`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHANTOM-VERSE-CPU-1

Installed `ashlr verse --port 7777` (Phantom.app, Bun 1.3.14 SEA, up 2d18h)
burned ~215 % CPU at idle. Root cause found, fixed, measured before/after on
the operator's real data.

## Diagnosis

- `sample 10536 5` on the installed process (read-only; never restarted or
  killed; `verse-remote.json` never read). The main thread was ~90 % idle. Two
  `Worker` threads were each ~100 % busy, which accounts for the 215 %. One
  worker thread id was replaced between samples minutes apart (worker
  recycled). Footprint was 8.1 GB.
- A fresh instance from source on loopback port 7794 (`--no-accounts`, GETs
  only) timed each projection against the real `~/.ashlr`:
  `/api/snapshot` **60 s → 503 timeout**, `/api/control` 18.4 s,
  `/api/fleet-activity` 14.1 s, `/api/fleet-state` 8.7 s, `/api/pulse` 7.6 s.
- The loop: the desktop keeps `/api/events` (1.5 s ticks) and 2–30 s polls open
  forever. `buildCachedSnapshot` has a 5 s TTL, and each miss asks the
  read-projection worker for a full rebuild. One real snapshot takes ~65–70 s,
  more than the worker's 60 s timeout. So the build is killed, the worker is
  terminated and respawned, and the next tick starts the same doomed build. A
  worker stays at 100 % forever and nothing is ever cached. Other slow
  projections keep the queue saturated the same way.
- `node --cpu-prof` of one `buildSnapshot` (69.5 s): 24 s re-scrubbing every
  inbox proposal (about a dozen secret regexes per diff, on every list), 16 s fleet
  status, 12 s re-parsing all Claude transcripts (3.3 GB, 3,672 files in 30 d)
  on every rollup, plus 6.7 s blocked (not CPU) on local-store lock contention
  with the live instance.

## Fix

1. **`src/core/web/read-projection-governor.ts` (new)**, wired in
   `server.ts` around `createReadProjectionWorker`:
   - Cost-scaled freshness: a build stays fresh for 9 × its own execution
     cost, which is ≤10 % duty per polled projection.
   - Cost is charged from when the build starts executing, not while it is
     queued in the serial worker.
   - Stale-while-revalidate for builds ≥ 1 s. Cheap ones still wait for fresh
     data.
   - Failure backoff: max(15 s × 2^n, 9 × failed cost), capped at 10 min. During
     backoff a request gets the last good value or a fast rejection. There is
     no backoff on INVALID_REQUEST/CLOSED.
   - `invalidate()` (after any authenticated mutation) clears values and
     backoff, and a build started before it cannot repopulate the cache.
   - Bounded to 64 entries.
2. **`src/core/inbox/store.ts`**: the stored-proposal scrub is memoized by a
   sha256 of the exact file bytes plus the HOME identity (2,048-entry LRU;
   files over 1 MiB are not retained). Structural validation, which touches
   the filesystem, still runs on every read. Each caller gets a
   `structuredClone`, so the memo cannot be poisoned. Scrubbing is not
   weakened: the same function produces the same output.
3. **`src/core/observability/usage-source.ts`**: per-file memo of extracted
   usage (token counts, model, timestamp, message key; never content).
   - An unchanged transcript is reused.
   - An append-only grown transcript is parsed from its last complete line.
   - Any rewrite (new inode, shrink, same-size mtime change, or changed
     256-byte tail fingerprint) is re-read from the start.
   - Bounded to 400k lines.
   - `eachLine` now splits on newline bytes, which fixes a latent corruption
     of multi-byte UTF-8 straddling a 64 KiB chunk and keeps long lines
     linear-time.
4. Docs: `docs/contracts/CONTRACT-M5.md` (memo semantics, test seam) and the
   `read-projections.ts` header.

## Measurements (real `~/.ashlr`, same machine)

- **Live A/B.** The same 150 s desktop-like poll (`snapshot` 1.5 s, `control`
  2 s, `fleet-activity` 5 s), with `sample` taken at t = 125 s for 10 s:
  - HEAD baseline (`git archive` export): read worker **96 % busy, ~104 % of a
    core total**, all 107 snapshot polls 503.
  - This change: **~1 % of a core total**.
- `collectUsageEvents(30 d)`, repeated call: 19.5 s → **0.78 s**, same
  event/token totals.
- `listProposalsDetailed` + `listProposals` (720 proposals): 3.7–4.7 s →
  1.2–2.3 s on repeat reads. Output digest is identical to HEAD.

## Commands run

- `sample <pid> 5` (installed and local instances).
- `node --cpu-prof --import tsx …` (projection profiles).
- Fresh `verse` instances on ports 7791/7794/7796/7797/7798 against real data,
  plus `curl` GETs.
- `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: PASS (tsc, authority
  drift, realio/verse-sync lints, 10/10 tests). **ESLint was SKIPPED:
  `node_modules/eslint` is absent in this worktree; Merge Gate lints on CI.**
- `npm run check:docs`: 0 errors.
- New suites: `test/web-read-projection-governor.test.ts` (17, including the
  idle-CPU budget tests), `test/usage-source-memo.test.ts` (9),
  `test/inbox-scrub-memo.test.ts` (4): **30/30 pass**, plus
  `test/m5.usage-source.test.ts` (46/46).
- Affected suites (219 files importing inbox store, usage-source, rollup,
  server, api or read-projections): see "Regression check" below.

## Regression check

Affected = 219 test files that import the inbox store, usage-source, rollup,
web server, api or read-projections.

- **Fixed tree, 4 of 5 batches (200 files):** 4,999 passed, 73 failed,
  8 skipped. The 73 failures are in 33 files. The 1 h background limit stopped
  the run before batch 5 (19 files); **those 19 files were not run**.
- **Compared on the unchanged HEAD tree** (`git archive` export):
  - `m420.remote-handoff-recovery`: the identical 7 tests fail on both trees.
  - `m23.store`: the identical 1 test fails on both trees.
  - `m13.dashboard`: same 5 s snapshot timeouts on both (2–3 tests, varies
    with load).
  - `m362.repair-handoff-journal` "concurrent journal burst": fails 3/3 in
    isolation on both trees. One baseline run in the batch passed it by luck.
    This is lock contention among 12 subprocess writers.
  - `m315.remote-handoff-truth`: the same failures on both trees.
  - `h3.atomic-writes` "N concurrent createProposal": flaky, a 30 s timeout
    under concurrent writers. In isolation the fixed tree went 1 pass / 1 fail
    and the baseline failed 2/2.
- **Not compared one by one (28 files).** These are mostly 5 s/30 s timeouts
  in daemon, judge and engine suites: grok/devin CLI confinement, gh, worker
  pool, fence-holder subprocesses (`m261`, `m405`, `h3` hang or time out in
  this sandbox). None of them exercises the changed behaviour beyond the
  scrub memo; the proposal/store ones checked above match baseline.

Merge Gate CI should be treated as the authoritative full run.

## Idle-CPU budget test

`test/web-read-projection-governor.test.ts`:
- **Simulated hour of 1.5 s polling.** Uses the measured costs: a 60 s
  always-timeout snapshot, a 65 s snapshot, 18 s control and 40 ms cheap. The
  test asserts worker duty stays under 15 % of one core in every case.
- **Real-CPU check (`process.cpuUsage`).** A governed 40 ms CPU-burning
  projection polled every 5 ms must stay under 30 % and under 0.4 × the
  ungoverned baseline (relative, so it is robust on loaded CI).

## Not done / follow-ups

- **The first build is still too slow on this home.** The 60 s worker timeout
  cap (`bounded-read-worker`, max 60 s by contract) still kills it, along with
  the worker's memos. The dashboard snapshot therefore stays unavailable here,
  as it already was at HEAD, but the CPU is now bounded. Options:
  - a longer timeout only for governed background refreshes;
  - keeping the worker alive on timeout;
  - making `buildFleetStatus` (16 s) and `listProposals` validation
    incremental.

  This needs an owner decision on the timeout contract.
- **Fleet-history trend fallback.** After 3 worker failures it switches to an
  inline main-thread mode that retries every request once the 15 s delay has
  passed, with no backoff. It was not the cause here (the main thread was
  ~90 % idle) but would benefit from the same governor.
- **Unidentified long-lived worker.** One of the two busy installed workers
  had been alive since launch, with no syscalls in its samples. Without JS
  symbols in the Bun SEA I could not tie it to a module for certain. The
  read-projection worker matches the measured loop, which this change fixes.
  Re-sample the installed app after it updates.
- `ps`/`top` were not permitted in this environment, so CPU was measured from
  `sample` thread activity.
- Pre-existing, environment-specific: CLI discovery opens
  `~/.local/bin/aw → ~/Desktop/...`, which blocked on macOS TCC in the agent
  shell. The A/B ran with `~/.local/bin` dropped from `PATH`.
- Nothing committed, pushed or published. No release scripts, workflows or
  security controls were touched.

## Net LOC

+1,021 / −48 (net **+973**) across 9 files: 5 modified, 4 new. About 560 of the added lines are tests; this notes file is excluded.

## Leftover temp files (deletion was denied in-session)

Delete these manually:
- `/private/tmp/verse-cpu-real`: profiles plus the dead local instances'
  startup JSON. That JSON contains their now-dead loopback tokens.
- `/private/tmp/verse-cpu-old`: HEAD export used as the baseline.
- `/tmp/bunexp`.
- `/private/tmp/aff-*.log`, `/private/tmp/f-*.log`,
  `/private/tmp/m*-*.log*`, `/private/tmp/runaff.sh`.
- The mktemp scratch HOME recorded in `/tmp/verse-cpu-scr`.
</details>

title: fix(release-train): drop the 60-minute HOURLY_MINUTES enqueue default
body:
## Why

After v3.30.31, the remaining train throttle on enqueueing a green release-please PR is `HOURLY_MINUTES = 60` in `observeTrain`. Hosted Release PR already uses `RELEASE_CADENCE_MINUTES` with a default of 5. The train still waited a full hour.

## What

- Replace `HOURLY_MINUTES = 60` with `DEFAULT_CADENCE_MINUTES = 5`.
- `observeTrain` reads `RELEASE_CADENCE_MINUTES` when set, otherwise the 5-minute default.
- Tests cover the default, env override, and invalid values.
- Token dispatch paths in `train.ts` are not changed.

## Notes

Does not weaken the clean-tree gate, move tags, or use admin bypass.

title: fix(ci): fail the quick job when generated files are stale
body:
## Why

v3.30.29 and v3.30.30 stopped in Desktop release smoke with `release smoke refused: source changed after build: M docs/llms.txt`. `node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs --check` already existed, but `npm run check:docs` only ran in the docs lane and the full Ubuntu authority shard. Both are skipped on the seconds-fast Merge Gate used for PRs, merge_group, and master pushes, so a new docs page could land without refreshing `docs/llms.txt`.

## Change

- Regenerated `docs/llms.txt` (adds FABLE-ORCHESTRATOR.md, PHANTOM-DISCOVERY.md, and intent-sweep-preservation-4235.md) so `npm run build` is a no-op write on this tree.
- Added a **Check generated files** step to the `quick` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It runs after Node setup on every `pull_request`, `merge_group`, and master push, including the source-identical fast path. It runs `node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs` and fails on any `git status --porcelain` dirty or untracked path.
- Read-only: no CI auto-commit, no path exemptions (including `docs/llms.txt`). The dirty-tree check in release smoke is unchanged and still has no exemption.
- Test in `test/m30.ci.test.ts` pins the step on the required fast path, with no `continue-on-error` and no commit/push/exemption.

Does not change train or auto-tag token/dispatch paths.

## Test

`npx vitest run test/m30.ci.test.ts -t "read-only generated-files"` passed. `node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs --check` exits 0 on this branch.

title: fix(release): dispatch with GITHUB_TOKEN, drop actions perm from App mints (fix-forward #4607)
body:
## Root cause

#4607 (`a8c04fe4`, merged 11:06 PM ET) asked `actions/create-github-app-token` for `permission-actions: write` on both the Auto-tag and Release train App mints, then used that token for workflow dispatches.

The ashlr-release GitHub App installation has `contents: write`, `metadata: read`, and `pull_requests: write` only. It has no `actions` permission. The mint therefore 422s at runtime, before a tag is created or the train can plan/apply.

This is a fix-forward of #4607, not a revert. Tag-ref dispatch (CI and attest on `vX.Y.Z`, npm publish still on `master`) is kept.

Security review (read-only, post-merge audit): `/workspace/eng/security/phantom-4607/REVIEW.md`. This PR implements recommended fix-forward (1): drop `permission-actions: write` from both App mints and keep dispatches on the job `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Diff summary

- `.github/workflows/auto-tag.yml`: add job-level `actions: write`; drop `permission-actions: write` from the App mint; dispatch release-gate CI with `${{ github.token }}`. The tag/draft step still uses the contents-only App token so the tag can trigger downstream workflows.
- `.github/workflows/release-train.yml`: drop `permission-actions: write` from the App mint. The train job already has `actions: write` on `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- `src/core/release/train.ts`: `releaseWriteUsesAppToken` again returns true only for draft PATCH and enqueue (`graphql`). Workflow dispatches use `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Tests in `test/release-train.test.ts`, `.github/tests/release-train.test.mjs`, and `.github/tests/release-cadence.test.mjs` updated to match, including that Auto-tag dispatch is not on the App token and the App mint does not request actions.

No App or org grant. No new `secrets.*` refs, no `id-token: write`, no `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run` trigger changes. Actions stay SHA-pinned. Required check names, signing, attestation, and KILL are unchanged.

## Timing

The 11:22 PM ET Auto-tag cron will likely fail on master before this merges (it mints the App token whenever checks are green and a tag is owed). The 12:07 AM ET Release train is the target: every train tick mints the App token with no `if:`, so it will fail until this lands.

## Checks run locally

- `actionlint` on `auto-tag.yml` and `release-train.yml`: pass
- YAML parse of both workflows: pass
- `vitest run test/release-train.test.ts`: 24 passed
- `node --test .github/tests/release-train.test.mjs .github/tests/release-cadence.test.mjs`: 36 passed

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-SELFLOOPBUSPROGRESS02SOLJ1` (pool: codex-local), single commit on base `9a643cfaf`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — fleet self-loop bus-progress (02solj1)

## Summary

Added opt-in `--bus-to <label> --bus-root <abs> --bus-run-id <token>` to
`ashlr fleet self-loop` so that each completed pass writes a compact progress
envelope to the existing durable bus (appendBusInbox).  No second bus, no new
verb, no core self-loop changes.  The 3-flag group is all-or-nothing: without
them the bus is untouched (existing behavior preserved).  Without `--apply`
ticks remain dry-run; the bus flags do not change dry-run semantics.

## Files changed

| File | Lines | Type |
|------|-------|------|
| `src/cli/fleet-self-loop.ts` | +178 −61 (net +117) | modified |
| `src/core/fleet/self-loop-bus-progress.ts` | +158 (new) | core module |
| `test/fleet-self-loop-bus-progress-02solj1.test.ts` | +328 (new) | tests |

**Total changed lines:** 603 (178 net CLI + 158 core + 328 test).

## Core module (`self-loop-bus-progress.ts`)

- `parseBusConfigGroup(to, root, runId)` — validates all three flags present
  or all absent; rejects partial groups, bad addresses, non-absolute roots,
  and invalid run-ids.
- `buildProgressEnvelope(cfg, pass, exitCode, state, cf, nd)` — constructs a
  `BusEnvelope` with `from: 'fleet-self-loop'`, `priority: 'P2'`, `ttl: 1h`,
  deterministic `id: ${runId}::pass-${pass}`, and a sanitized body containing
  only `kind`, `runId`, `pass`, `exitCode`, `state`,
  `consecutiveFailures`, `nextDelayMs`.  No raw reports, no paths, no
  exception text.
- `postProgressEnvelope(envelope, options)` — delegates to `appendBusInbox`.
- `readDeliveredEnvelopes(options)` — delegates to `listBusInboxAfter`.

## CLI changes (`fleet-self-loop.ts`)

- Three new flags parsed in the existing flag loop: `--bus-to`, `--bus-root`,
  `--bus-run-id`.  Partial groups rejected before any pass runs (exit 2).
- `--help` now prints full usage (including bus flags) and exits 0.
- A combined `onPass` callback is wired into `runSelfLoop`: when bus flags
  are absent, no bus is touched; when present, the envelope is built and
  posted after the existing stream output (if `--stream`).  An accepted
  `'duplicate'` counts as delivery (no error); any other status sets
  `observerError` (bus-unavailable/bus-full etc.) and produces exit 1
  without re-running the tick.

## Test results

```
vitest run test/fleet-self-loop-bus-progress-02solj1.test.ts --no-file-parallelism
  → 16 passed (16), 0 failed
```

Existing related tests (stream, failure-backoff, sleep-budget): 24 passed.

The single failing test in `test/fleet-self-loop-02soly1.test.ts`
("runs the first pass immediately, then one interval apart, never overlapping")
was already failing with the original code (expected sleep `[1000,1000,1000]`
vs actual `[1000,1000,500]` — the 3rd sleep is correctly capped by the 2500 ms
deadline minus 2000 ms elapsed = 500 ms).  This is a pre-existing assertion
error, not introduced by this change.

## Verification commands run

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-self-loop-bus-progress-02solj1.test.ts --no-file-parallelism
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-self-loop-stream-02solc1.test.ts test/fleet-self-loop-failure-backoff-02solh2.test.ts test/fleet-self-loop-sleep-budget-02solg2.test.ts --no-file-parallelism
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
```

ESLint was unrunnable in this worktree (missing `../lib/cli` module).

## Limitations

- The `'full'` and `'unavailable'` transport paths are tested through the
  existing `bus-inbox` test suite; the self-loop integration test for a
  pre-filled 1024-message inbox was omitted because filling 1024 messages
  through sequential file I/O exceeds practical test timeouts (~3 minutes).
  The CLI code path is correct: any non-posted/non-duplicate result from
  `postProgressEnvelope` sets `observerError` and returns exit 1.
- ESLint validation could not be completed (missing build artifact).
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-SELFLOOPSTOPFILE02SOLD2
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-SELFLOOPSTOPFILE02SOLD2` (pool: devin), single commit on base `004e366b4`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/CODEOWNERS .github/scripts/ci-source-binding.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-SELFLOOPSTOPFILE02SOLD2

Graceful memory-backpressure / autonomous-operation stop order for
`ashlr fleet self-loop`: a supervising agent can stop admission to an
existing self-loop by placing an explicit stop file — no PID discovery, no
process signal, and the in-flight self-tick always finishes.

## Behavior

- New optional flag `--stop-file <absolute path>` on the existing self-loop
  verb. Validated before any tick runs: the flag may appear once, the value
  must be an absolute path, and it must contain no control characters
  (code points `< 0x20` and `0x7f`); violations exit 2 with usage.
- Core seam (`src/core/fleet/self-loop.ts`): `runSelfLoop` accepts optional
  `checkStop` (async admission-stop verdict `'continue' | 'stop'`, awaited
  before every pass including the first) and `stopObserved` (a factory raced
  with each inter-tick sleep so a stop seen while waiting wakes admission
  promptly). A `checkStop` verdict of `'stop'` ends admission with a bounded
  summary carrying `termination: 'stop-file'` and zero additional ticks — a
  preexisting file therefore yields `ticks: 0`. A `checkStop` rejection ends
  the loop with `termination: 'stop-check-error'` (never silently launching
  another pass); the CLI exits 1 on that termination.
- `watchSelfLoopStopFile(path)` wires the concrete file source read-only
  (`lstat` only; the file is never created or removed by the loop): `ENOENT`
  => continue, existing path => stop, any other filesystem error => reject.
  One event-driven `fs.watch` on the parent directory (no busy polling;
  observed latency is watch latency, well under the required one second),
  each event confirmed by the same existence read. Once fired, exactly one
  observation is delivered and the view never settles again, so the loop can
  never spin; one bounded watch + one promise per run, released in `finally`
  (idempotent `close()`). While the option is absent, behavior is exactly as
  before, including first-pass semantics.
- Output distinguishes all four exit reasons: JSON `termination` is one of
  `duration` / `interrupted` / `stop-file` / `stop-check-error`
  (`observer-error` preserved from SOLC1), human output prints `DONE` /
  `INTERRUPTED` / `STOPPED-BY-FILE` / `STOP-CHECK-ERROR` (and the preserved
  `OBSERVER-ERROR`). Exit codes: 0 success/no-failure (stop-file is a
  graceful order), 1 on any failed pass / observer error / stop-check error,
  2 on usage.

## Upstream integration

origin/master moved during the task: the previously pending
SELFLOOPPROGRESS02SOLC1 (`--stream` onPass progress, `observer-error`
termination) merged at 6577cb03d. The worktree was fast-forwarded and the
stop-file change rebased onto it; both features coexist (combined usage
line, shared `label` mapping, combined exit-code expression). Fresh-master
sleep/admission structure, first-pass admission, and `sanitizePublicJson`
handling are unchanged. No panics on shared hunks; SOLC1's semantics
verified by running its own suite.

## Validation (all ran with `HOME=$(mktemp -d)`, sequentially, no real long sleeps)

- `npm run test:ci -- test/fleet-self-loop-stop-file-02sold2.test.ts` —
  10 passed / 10 (new suite: preexisting file prevents first pass; creation
  during idle wait wakes admission promptly without resolving the sleep;
  creation mid-pass lets the pass finish with zero additional passes;
  missing file preserves 3-tick repetition and is never created; ENOTDIR
  path error stops admission at exit 1 with `stop-check-error`; relative /
  empty / missing-value / duplicate / control-character `--stop-file` all
  exit 2 with zero ticks; human-output label distinction; core-seam direct
  tests for gating order, rejection, prompt wake, and watch hygiene).
- `npm run test:ci -- test/fleet-self-loop-02soly1.test.ts` — 16 passed / 16
  (existing behavior preserved).
- `npm run test:ci -- test/fleet-self-loop-stream-02solc1.test.ts` —
  9 passed / 9 (merged progress support preserved).
- `npx eslint src/core/fleet/self-loop.ts src/cli/fleet-self-loop.ts
  test/fleet-self-loop-stop-file-02sold2.test.ts` — clean (this worktree's
  `node_modules/eslint` was missing its `lib/` directory from install;
  repaired by copying `lib/` from the identical eslint@9.39.5 in the local
  guardian-phantom worktree; no packages were installed or changed).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: tsgo is not present in
  this worktree, so per instructions the fallback ran: `npx tsc --noEmit -p
  tsconfig.json` — completed in the foreground, exit 0.

Commands intentionally not run: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, builds,
package installs, full test suite (per task constraints).

## Limitations

- If the stop file is created, observed, and then deleted before the loop's
  own admission re-read, admission continues (missing file means continue)
  and prompt wake-on-creation degrades to per-boundary checks (the one-shot
  fused observation is consumed); each pass boundary still re-reads the
  file.
- A parent-directory watch that cannot be established (e.g. missing parent,
  resource exhaustion) degrades to the per-pass read only; an unreadable
  stop path still fails loudly via `checkStop` as `stop-check-error`.
- Precedence when conditions coincide: at a pass boundary the deadline or an
  abort ends admission before the stop check runs, so those report
  `duration` / `interrupted`; an explicit stop found at the boundary reports
  `stop-file`; a failing stop read reports `stop-check-error`.
- The single-line usage summary lists `[--stop-file <abs>]`; README/docs
  updates were out of scope for this job.

## Diff

`git diff HEAD --stat` (HEAD == origin/master 6577cb03d; changes staged
only, nothing committed):

```
 src/cli/fleet-self-loop.ts                     |  42 ++++-
 src/core/fleet/self-loop.ts                    | 107 ++++++++++-
 test/fleet-self-loop-stop-file-02sold2.test.ts | 238 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 378 insertions(+), 9 deletions
```

Net LOC: +378 / -9 = 387 changed lines (≤ 400 cap). Only the three named
paths plus this note are touched; nothing under `.github/`, no CODEOWNERS,
manifest, or release-tooling changes.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-CHANGELOGFRAGMENTS02

## Summary

`src/core/fleet/collision-free-edits.ts` already diverts a fleet changelog
edit into `changelog.d/<id>.<kind>.md`, but nothing wrote or folded those
fragments. This job adds both halves:

- **`src/core/fleet/changelog-fold.ts`** (new) — `listFragments(dir, fs)`
  reads `changelog.d/*.md` through an injected fs, validates
  `<id>.<kind>.md` names against `CHANGELOG_FRAGMENT_KINDS` (other names are
  ignored), skips symlinks, non-files, >16 KiB files, unreadable/misshapen
  content with reasons, and sorts by kind order then id.
  `foldChangelog(text, fragments)` is pure text surgery: it finds the FIRST
  `## [x.y.z] — Unreleased` heading (none → unchanged text + skipped reason
  `no-unreleased-section`), appends each fragment's `- ` bullet lines under
  the matching `### Heading`, creates a missing heading at the end of the
  Unreleased section before the next `## `, never duplicates an exact
  bullet, and never touches anything outside the section. A dated section
  below stays byte-identical (asserted in tests).
  `unreleasedSection(text)` extracts the section for previews.
- **`src/cli/fleet-changelog.ts`** (new) — `cmdFleetChangelog`:
  - `ashlr fleet changelog add --id <id> --kind <kind> <entry>...` renders
    via `renderChangelogFragment` and writes with the `wx` flag — an
    existing fragment is refused (exit 1), never overwritten. 1–32 entries.
  - `ashlr fleet changelog fold [--apply] [--json]` — without `--apply`
    prints folded/skipped paths and the new top section, writing nothing;
    with `--apply` writes CHANGELOG.md then deletes only folded fragments.
  - `--root <abs>` on both; default is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of
    cwd. Exit 0 ok / 1 refused-or-failed / 2 usage; `--help` prints usage.
- **`src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`** — regenerated with
  `node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`; adds the `changelog` loader and
  repairs a pre-existing drift (`self-loop` was on master but unlisted).

## Commands an agent should run

```sh
# Add an entry without touching CHANGELOG.md:
npm run dev -- fleet changelog add --id <job-id> --kind fixed "fixed the thing"

# Preview the fold (writes nothing):
npm run dev -- fleet changelog fold [--json]

# Fold all fragments into the top Unreleased section and delete them:
npm run dev -- fleet changelog fold --apply

# Against a scratch root:
npm run dev -- fleet changelog fold --apply --root /abs/repo
```

## Verification

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/changelog-fold.test.ts` — 14/14 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-changelog-cli.test.ts` — 7/7 pass

- `npx eslint src/core/fleet/changelog-fold.ts src/cli/fleet-changelog.ts src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts test/changelog-fold.test.ts test/fleet-changelog-cli.test.ts` — clean (exit 0)

Dependencies were prepared with `npm run install:worktree` (pnpm 10.28.2,
shared store) — the worktree's node_modules was incomplete and eslint would
not run without it. No commits, no version bumps; `git fetch origin master`
re-verified the registry hunk applies cleanly on the newest master.

# RQ-NODE-6-TENANCY: identity layer (person, team, org)

## Summary

- **New `src/core/tenancy/`**
  - `owner.ts` (pure): `Owner {kind: person|team|org, id}`, `parseOwner`, `ownerKey`, `visibleTo`, and `TenancyError(message, fix)`.
  - `index.ts`:
    - `whoami()` gets the person from local auth only: the OS user, or `$ASHLR_HOME/teams/owner.json`. It reads no token and spawns no `gh`.
    - Teams come from the local team bus. A person counts as a member only after joining from a human terminal or being invited; a message posted under a claimed `--as` name does not count.
    - Orgs live in `$ASHLR_HOME/tenancy/orgs.json` (written atomically, 0600).
    - Also exports `orgList`, `orgAdd` (idempotent), `assertOwnerAccess` and `assertTeamAccess`.
    - Output is sorted and has no timestamps, so it is deterministic.
- **Nodes, jobs and leases (`src/core/drive/nodes`)**
  - `join(nodeId, owner?)` and `enqueue(jobId, owner?)` record an owner, and `parseState` validates it.
  - `claim` throws `TenancyError` (with a fix) when the job's owner differs from the worker node's owner. Unowned only matches unowned. On refusal nothing is committed.
  - `complete` runs `scrubSecrets` on the result before storing it, since results are shared logs.
- **Forum and context packs (`src/core/teams`)**
  - Every `phm_team_*` MCP tool refuses a team you are not a member of. The error text includes the fix.
  - `phm team view|join|claim|release|say` do the same check.
  - A team with no members yet stays open. This keeps the default bus and the existing MCP flows working.
  - The existing `assertNoSecrets` still keeps secrets out of forum posts and packs; the new tests cover it.
- **Refactor:** I split `localHumanName()` out of `localHumanActor()` so agents can resolve the person they act for without getting approval authority.
- **CLI:** new `phm whoami [--json]` and `phm org list|add <org> [--team <t>] [--json]` (`src/cli/tenancy.ts`).
  - Errors print `error:`/`fix:`, or `{error, fix}` with `--json`.
  - Exit codes: 0 success, 1 tenancy error, 2 usage.
  - Also wired into `index.ts`, completions and `help.ts`.
- **Docs:** new `docs/TENANCY.md` (plain English, copy-paste example, enforcement table, limits), plus entries in `docs/llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/README.md`.
  - I regenerated `docs/cli.md`. It was already stale on master, so the diff also includes unrelated drift (graph, self-swap, lanes caps and so on).
- **Tests:** new `test/tenancy.test.ts` with 12 tests. They cover cross-tenant isolation for jobs and leases, logs (secret scrubbing), forum threads, context packs and secrets, plus whoami/org determinism, the CLI JSON and error shapes, corrupt config, and spoofed `--as` names.

- The NODECAPS router should filter candidate nodes with `visibleTo` / `ownerKey` before calling `claim`. `claim` is the backstop.
- `phm team say/claim --as <name>` still sets the displayed author, as before. Tenancy checks ignore it, but removing `--as` is a separate hardening.

title: Add a calm fleet mission briefing
body:
## What & why The desktop at `/verse/` now has one place to see the Mac fleet. Mission opens on a single briefing: whether everything is moving, what merged this hour (with pull links), and what needs a look. Jobs, recent choices, time left, main branches, incidents, memory, and the leaders' plan stay one click deeper. Agents read the same document. `ashlr fleet mission --json` and `GET /api/verse/fleet/runs/mission` both return `fleet.mission.v1`. The route sits on the existing loopback fleet-runs API. Missing files stay unknown, and free text is scrubbed before it is shown. It builds on the readers the app already trusts (runs directory, lane models, the jobs ledger, the usage journal, and the memory view) and only adds the files those readers do not cover: `queue/resources.json`, `supervisor/status-*.md`, `leader/INCIDENTS.md`, and `leader/VISION.md`. [Mission briefing: something needs a look, two pulls merged, four things to notice](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-124196c5-6eb9-5738-aaa4-27c90a947825/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmission-overview.png) [What is running, one click down: Personal Codex, Devin, and local models](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-124196c5-6eb9-5738-aaa4-27c90a947825/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmission-running.png) [The plan, one click down: this week](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-124196c5-6eb9-5738-aaa4-27c90a947825/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmission-plan.png) ## How it was verified - `npx vitest run test/fleet-mission.test.ts` — fixture fleet, missing directory, usage-journal fallback, symlink refusal, secret scrub, CLI, and the route - `npm run test:web -- src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-mission` and the fleet hub tile tests - `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passed - `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: file selection, eslint on changed files, and backend `tsgo --noEmit` passed. Web `tsgo` fails on current `master` with the same pre-existing diagnostics (FleetRuns fixtures and unrelated notification types). None of those errors are in the mission files. ## Safety checklist - [x] No new outward capability. The view and the CLI are read-only. - [x] No new runtime dependencies - [x] Secrets are scrubbed; paths and prompts do not render - [x] Loopback only: the route is on the existing verse API ## Notes Open it from Fleet, or with the Mission pane (`Mod+Alt+K`). The hub lists Mission first. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added a Fleet Mission briefing in the fleet hub, showing fleet health, items needing attention, recent merges, and expandable details for jobs, decisions, resources, main branches, incidents, memory, and plans. - Added a read-only `fleet mission` command with formatted and JSON output. - The briefing refreshes automatically while open and supports manual refresh. Missing or unavailable information is shown as unreported rather than assumed. - **Documentation** - Documented the Fleet Mission command and its JSON output.

title: Add a fleet forum for agent coordination
body:
## What & why Agents in the fleet now have a shared forum: channels (`#goals`, `#incidents`, `#reviews`, `#releases`, `#growth`), threads, replies, and `@mentions` that wake another agent through the existing local bus. Structured posts cover proposals, commitments, review requests, blockers, and retros. A commitment has an owner and a deadline. `phm forum sweep` (or `phm forum tick` on the leader's schedule) flags an overdue one in `#incidents`, wakes the owner once, and reassigns the queued job through the job pool. If there is no queued job, it drops a new one. A standup retro on `#goals` reports merges, main health, releases, and star growth. The same store is reachable three ways: the typed service, `phm forum`, and the `phantom_forum` MCP tool. The desktop Forum pane and the phone Forum screen are read-only. Telegram and email steering stay where they are; once the forum file exists, a channel message from a bound principal (Mason, or someone Mason invited) is copied into `#goals`. Posts are data. They are never passed to a shell. Agent keys come from `PHANTOM_FORUM_AGENT_KEYS`, a private key file, or the macOS keychain, and are never written into the repo. Mason is the only human until `phm forum invite`. Mention loops and post floods are suppressed. Writes go through the MCP kill switch; reads stay available. ## How it was verified - `npx tsc --noEmit` (backend) clean - `npx eslint` on the forum sources clean - `npx vitest run test/fleet-forum.test.ts test/fleet-forum-sim.test.ts` — 9 tests, including a two-agent simulation that creates a commitment, flags it when overdue, reassigns `RQ-PHX-FORUMJOB1` in `ready.tsv` once, and does not move it again - `npm run test:web` for the forum pane, board, and phone screen - `npm run check:docs` clean - `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: eslint and backend typecheck passed. Web typecheck failed on existing errors in unrelated files (`deriveUpdateNotifications`, `window-title`, `palette-workers`, and others). Those files are unchanged here. No new runtime dependencies. [Fleet forum desktop view](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-d480f7f3-fcda-545c-bc87-44dd48504d5d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Ffleet-forum-desktop.png) [Fleet forum phone width](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-d480f7f3-fcda-545c-bc87-44dd48504d5d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Ffleet-forum-phone.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a Fleet Forum for browsing discussions across channels, viewing recent posts, and tracking overdue commitments. * The forum is available in desktop and mobile interfaces, with channel selection and manual refresh on mobile. * Added command-line and MCP access for reading and managing forum posts, commitments, standups, and channel bridges. * Added optional mirroring of forum posts to Telegram or Discord and a read-only forum API.

title: bridge: RQ-SELFOPT-PROMPT-OPT
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SELFOPT-PROMPT-OPT` (pool: devin), single commit on base `4c1199027`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SELFOPT-PROMPT-OPT

Job: RQ-SELFOPT-PROMPT-OPT (P1, pool=devin, tier=mid, repo=phantom, lead=Core, bet=bold)
Branch: `codex-bridge/RQ-SELFOPT-PROMPT-OPT` — every change left uncommitted per instructions.

> optimize job prompts and policy from outcome logs. A/B test prompt variants per
> job class, scored by the eval harness (depends on RQ-SELFOPT-EVAL-HARNESS);
> promote a winner only on a significant lift. Acceptance: one promoted variant
> with before/after numbers on the dashboard.

## What shipped

**Dependency ported (RQ-SELFOPT-EVAL-HARNESS, from sibling commit `0f23d1d69`, unmerged):**
the offline router-eval harness — `src/core/eval/router-eval.ts`, `src/cli/eval-router.ts`,
`phm eval router`, the frozen `benchmarks/router-eval/` day, `docs/router/eval.md` and
`test/router-eval-harness.test.ts`. Honest replay semantics: recorded arms reuse logged
outcomes; changed decisions score only against frozen counterfactual `arms`, else
`unobserved` — never estimated.

**Prompt A/B + promotion (this job):**
- `src/core/eval/prompt-variants.ts` — prompt variant registry (`prompt:plain`,
  `prompt:adaptive`) with real dispatch templates, `classifyJobClass` (docs/tests/secrets),
  and `assignPromptVariant`: promoted class → winner; active experiment → deterministic
  SHA-256 bucket by job id; unmatched → incumbent behavior.
- `src/core/eval/prompt-ab.ts` — per-class A/B replay through `evaluateRouterPolicy`;
  promotion gate requires min resolved cohort per arm, unobserved-rate cap, disjoint
  Wilson-95% intervals (significant lift), and a cost-per-merged-PR regression bound.
  Holds are named: `insufficient-data`, `not-significant`, `thin-coverage`,
  `cost-regression`, `no-lift`.
- `src/core/eval/prompt-promotions.ts` — durable registry at
  `$ASHLR_HOME/eval/prompts/promotions.json`, atomic tmp+rename writes, malformed input
  reads as absent, `mergePromotions` replaces only the classes the new report covers.
- `src/cli/eval-prompts.ts` — `phm eval prompts --dataset <jobs.jsonl> [--spec] [--promote]
  [--write] [--check] [--json]`; markdown or JSON report, `--check` is the regression gate.
- `src/cli/pulse.ts` — new "Prompt variants" dashboard section (before→after merge rate,
  cohort sizes, lift) plus additive `promptVariants` field in `pulse --json`, same pattern
  as `forecast`/`governance`.
- `benchmarks/prompt-ab/` — deterministic `generate.mjs`, frozen `jobs.jsonl`
  (65 lines, sha256 `de148860…dbd55`), `experiment.json`, committed `promotions.json`,
  `report.md`, README.
- Docs: `docs/router/prompt-ab.md` + index rows in `docs/README.md`, `docs/HUB-REFERENCE.md`,
  `src/cli/help.ts`; `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` + `docs/cli.md` regenerated (they were stale on
  master; generator output must match exactly).

## Acceptance evidence

```
phm eval prompts --dataset benchmarks/prompt-ab/jobs.jsonl --promote
  docs    PROMOTED prompt:adaptive   33.3% (n=30) → 77.8% (n=27)  +44.4 pts  CIs disjoint
  tests   held  not-significant      61.5% → 66.7% (+5.1 pts, intervals overlap)
  secrets held  insufficient-data    6 resolved per arm

phm pulse
  Prompt variants  promoted by prompt-ab-2026-10-28
    docs: prompt:adaptive  33.3% → 77.8% merge (n 30→27)  +44.4 pts
```

`--check benchmarks/prompt-ab/promotions.json` exits 0 on replay, 1 on drift (tested).

## Commands run

- `npm ci` — PASS
- `npm run typecheck` — PASS (root `tsc --noEmit` + web tsconfig)
- `npm run check:docs` — PASS (0 errors, 227 local links, 0 external requests)
- `npx eslint <all 14 touched files>` — PASS (0 problems)
- `npm run lint` — FAIL: 1 error, `.github/tests/ci-mac-rotation.test.mjs` `'URL' is not
  defined`. Pre-existing on `dd3ca503a`; `.github/**` is out of scope. 203 warnings,
  all pre-existing.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) ASHLR_HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run <17 touched suites>` —
  **1054 passed / 3 failed** (files: 16 passed / 1 failed). All 3 failures in
  `test/role-completion.test.ts` (real-io lane): "Selected native account launch
  unavailable", 60 s transport timeout — native-account environment, unrelated to this
  diff. Post-fix re-run of the 3 new suites: **70/70 pass**
  (`router-eval-harness`, `prompt-ab`, `pulse-prompt-variants`).
- `phm eval prompts --dataset benchmarks/prompt-ab/jobs.jsonl --check
  benchmarks/prompt-ab/promotions.json` — PASS (exit 0), under both the builtin
  spec and `--spec benchmarks/prompt-ab/experiment.json`.
- `npm run gate -- --base HEAD` — build PASS, docs PASS, realio-lane PASS,
  typecheck-web PASS, verse-sync-io PASS. Pre-existing failures: `test-names` (21
  baseline duplicate names), `eslint` (the `.github` error above), `first-paint`
  (chat 358.6 > 354 KB, phone 250.1 > 250 KB — this diff adds no web code),
  `tests-web` (`src/web-ui/routes/verse/VerseApp.test.tsx`), `tests-backend`
  (`verse-server-wiring-310` timing flake, `verse-session-engine` real-io,
  `authority-codeowners-310b` — see below).

## Known owner-follow-up (not weakening anything)

`test/router-eval-harness.test.ts` matches the `tier1-test` rule by name (the `router`
token in `TIER1_TEST_STEMS` deliberately over-matches so router-adjacent tests route to
owner review). CODEOWNERS regeneration is `ASHLR_UPDATE_CODEOWNERS=1 npx vitest run
test/authority-codeowners-310b.test.ts`, but `.github/CODEOWNERS` is off-limits here;
the assertion already failed on master for 4 other unowned files. Kept the accurate name
rather than dodge the stem. Same constraint the sibling harness branch shipped under.

## Bug caught by the `--check` gate during final verification

`DEFAULT_PROMPT_EXPERIMENT` was a raw spec literal — `compileClass` (inside
`parsePromptExperimentSpec`) never ran, so `match.task` regexes were absent and
`classifyPromptJob` silently dropped the task matcher. Every job classified into the
first class (`docs`): the builtin replay held docs (all 65 jobs in one arm cohort,
tests/secrets empty), and — worse — dispatch-time `assignPromptVariant` would have
routed *every* job to the docs winner. Fixed two ways: the builtin constant is now
built through `parsePromptExperimentSpec`, and `classifyPromptJob` compiles
`match.task` when `taskRe` is absent so an unvalidated spec object can never skip a
declared matcher again. Regression test added in `test/prompt-ab.test.ts`.

## Nearby pre-existing drift fixed along the way

- `completions.ts`: added `queue` to `fleet` (dispatched to router-queue.js since before
  this change) and `bus` to `devin` (accepted by `devin.ts`). Repairs the
  `doc-facts`/`cli-completions-subcommands` failures present on master.
- Regenerated `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` + `docs/cli.md`; absorbs pre-existing staleness
  (`config list`, `drive`, `worktrees`, topic hints) — required for the drift test.

## Net LOC

30 files: **+3,734 / −36 (net +3,698)** —
16 tracked-diff files (+1,828/−36) + 14 new files (+1,906 incl. this file):
3 core modules, 1 CLI, 2 test suites, 1 docs page, 6 benchmark artifacts, BRIDGE_NOTES.

## Not done / boundaries

- No commit, push, tag, or publish; no `.github/**` or CODEOWNERS edits.
- `assignPromptVariant` is exposed for the dispatch seam (`buildCloudPrompt` wraps
  `task.prompt`); wiring dispatchers to consult the registry is the follow-up slice.
- `fleet optimize-prompt` (GEPA judge/strategist evolution) is a different layer — no
  collision; this feature targets per-job-class dispatch prompt variants.
</details>

## What landed

- `src/core/ecosystem/changelog-document.ts` (new): pure deterministic render
  layer. `asOf` is a required input so identical inputs produce byte-identical
  output. `--since` accepts `<N>d`, `<N>h` or an ISO instant and is inclusive;
  undated (unreleased) changelog sections always pass. Document entries omit
  `body` (the index keeps `url` to full text), which bounds the committed
  JSON artifact. `recent14d` is the fixed 14-day llms-style summary computed
  over the emitted document so every count is derivable from
  `repositories[].changes`. Markdown render: header totals, "Last 14 days",
  "Pending release notes" (undated sections), per-repo listings in strategic
  tier order, degraded-source notices. All text runs through dash
  normalization (`U+2010..U+2015` -> ASCII) so artifacts contain no em/en
  dashes.
- `src/cli/ecosystem.ts`: new `changelog` subcommand with `--json`,
  `--since`, `--as-of`, `--root`, `--max-pages` (1-100), `--write`.
  `--write` writes `ECOSYSTEM_CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/ecosystem-changelog.json`
  into the nearest repo root. Exit 1 when any source is incomplete; exit 2 on
  usage errors; `--help` works without touching the network.

  version + normalized heading (Phantom's many `[Unreleased] - M<N>`
