body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PARITYROUTERTASKQ7` (pool: devin), single commit on base `4c1199027`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** src/core/routing/policy.ts src/core/routing/router.ts src/core/routing/task-bandit.ts src/core/routing/types.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PARITYROUTERTASKQ7

## Summary

Task-aware bandit lane inside the EXISTING seat router (no second router):
a task classifier maps `(class, size, risk, repo)` onto contextual Thompson
draws over `(engine, model, effort)` arms spanning Claude Code, Codex, Grok,
Devin and local/oMLX, rewarded on merged-and-green PRs per token, gated by
the #938 LP pacing constraint, with risky classes frontier-only per #926 —
all behind an off-by-default flag on `RouteOptions.taskBandit`.

- New `src/core/routing/task-bandit.ts` (~780 LOC, pure, browser-safe, no
  `node:` imports): the 13-arm catalog over `TASK_BANDIT_ENGINES`
  (`claude|codex|grok|devin|local`; `claude-api` is never an arm), the
  classifier and four-level context-cell keys (exact → repo-free →
  size-free → global, every outcome folds into all four so cold cells
  borrow strength), Beta posteriors + deterministic Thompson draws
  (mulberry32 seeded by FNV-1a(seed, itemKey)), the reward
  `min(1, tokenNorm / max(tokens, tokenFloor))` on merged-AND-green only,
  `pacingAllowance` wrapping `resources/pacing.ts paceWindow` (absent map =
  constraint inactive; unlisted/invalid pool = fail closed), the
  `planTaskBandit` pure decision half, the `phantom-task-bandit-outcome/v1`
  settled-evidence schema with strict row validation, `recordTaskOutcome`
  for live updates, and `replayTaskBandit` — a rejection-sampling
  counterfactual estimator producing the acceptance report.
- `src/core/routing/router.ts`: previous `routeSeat` body extracted
  unchanged into exported `routeSeatCore`; `routeSeat` consults the bandit
  only for `req.autonomous && opts.taskBandit`. `shadow` annotates the
  static decision; `enforce` tries each drawn arm's engine subset in θ
  order through `routeSeatCore` (every eligibility/headroom/context-fit/
  funding/lane check intact — Devin's fleet-lane verdict included) and
  HOLDS rather than falling back when no drawn engine yields a seat.
- `src/core/routing/types.ts`: additive contracts — `TaskBanditEngine`,
  `TaskRiskClass`, `TaskEffort`, `TaskSizeBucket`, `TaskBanditContext`,
  `TaskArm`, `SeatBanditNote`, and optional `SeatDecision.bandit` (absent
  entirely when the flag is off).
- `src/core/routing/policy.ts`: `TASK_BANDIT_ENGINES`,
  `FRONTIER_TASK_ENGINES` (the hosted subset minus `local`), the guards,
  `TaskBanditMode` (`off|shadow|enforce`), `TaskBanditConfig`,
  `DEFAULT_TASK_BANDIT_CONFIG` and `parseTaskBanditConfig` — strict
  salvage, fail closed; `enabled: true` without a valid mode parses to
  `shadow`, so flipping the flag can never silently reroute.

## Safety properties (all tested)

- Flag-off identity: absent/disabled/off config, or a non-autonomous
  request, produces a byte-identical `SeatDecision` with no `bandit` field.
- Unknown engines are never arms and never selected: a `claude-api`-only
  fleet holds in enforce mode; replay counts `watson`/`claude-api` logged
  arms as `unknownArmRecords` and they are never drawn.
- Risky stays frontier-only: `riskClass 'high'` or a merge/merge-rights/
  publish hint admits no `local` arm; a local-only fleet on a risky task
  holds in enforce rather than relaxing the gate; credentialed work holds
  outright.
- LP pacing is eligibility, not ranking: floored or unproven pools lose
  their arms; the bandit can never spend past the plan.

## Acceptance

- `replayTaskBandit` on `test/fixtures/task-bandit/history.jsonl`
  (227 synthetic records, seeded deliberately expensive-heavy):
  kept=19 on-policy records, tokens-per-merge **231,029 vs 410,183** for
  the logged policy (-44%), merge rate **1.000 vs 0.855** — lower tokens
  per merged PR at a no-worse merge rate. `unknownArmRecords=2`, `held=3`,
  every drawn arm is a catalog arm, and the report is deterministic
  (identical replay → identical report).
- `test/task-bandit.test.ts` — 86 tests covering flag parsing, classifier
  buckets, reward math, posterior updates, seeded determinism, pacing
  gate, frontier-only risky work, credentials hold, unknown engines,
  shadow vs enforce through the real `routeSeat`, and the fixture replay.

## Commands run

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean (twice; final after all edits)
- `npm run check:docs` — `ok: true`, 0 errors
- `npx eslint src/core/routing/{task-bandit,router,policy,types}.ts
  test/task-bandit.test.ts` — clean, 0 findings
- `npm run lint` — 1 error + 203 warnings, all pre-existing on the branch
  (the only error is `.github/tests/ci-mac-rotation.test.mjs` no-undef from
  an earlier bridge commit — off-limits, reproduced identical at base)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/task-bandit.test.ts
  test/routing-seat-router.test.ts test/m15.router-replay.test.ts
  test/routing-router-weights.test.ts test/routing-interactive-scope.test.ts
  test/m21.policy.test.ts test/router-typing.test.ts
  test/dispatch-router-310b.test.ts test/routing-budget-api.test.ts
  test/routing-budget-store.test.ts test/router-calibration.test.ts
  test/routing-readiness-314.test.ts test/routing-subscription-failclosed.test.ts
  test/routing-capacity-history.test.ts test/router-current-claude-models.test.ts
  test/routing-calibration-properties.test.ts test/m404.policy-result-surfaces.test.ts`
  — **17 files, 518 tests, all pass**
- `npm run gate` — see below
- `npm ci` — required repair: the worktree's node_modules was a partial
  install (eslint missing lib/, react-dom cjs truncated); unrelated to code

## Gate result

`npm run gate` (related mode, base origin/master @ 4c1199027):
- PASS: build, typecheck-web, docs, realio-lane, verse-sync-io
- FAIL (all reproduced identical at base; none caused by this change):
  - `test-names` — 22 within-file duplicate test names vs baseline 21, all
    in files this change does not touch (rq-backlog-gen, steward-schedule,
    drive-cli-bridge, pool-budget-store, …)
  - `eslint` — the single pre-existing `.github/` error above
  - `first-paint` — chat 358.6 KB vs 354 KB and phone 250.1 vs 250 KB
    budgets, IDENTICAL at base (verified by stashing this change and
    rebuilding; the bandit code lands in a lazily-loaded chunk, not the
    first-paint critical path)
  - `tests-web` — mass `localStorage is undefined` TypeErrors in `.tsx`
    component suites; reproduced identical at base on a stashed clean tree
- `tests-backend` — the related suite (vitest import-graph selection over
  the routing hub) ran 680+ test files with zero file failures while this
  report was written and was still running; the hermetic `test:ci` run of
  the 17 directly-touched suites (518 tests) is the authoritative coverage
  above.

## Pass/fail counts

- Touched/affected backend tests: **518 passed, 0 failed** (17 files,
  hermetic runner) — includes `test/task-bandit.test.ts` (86) and the
  seat-router, router-replay, policy, weights, interactive-scope, dispatch,
  budget API/store, calibration and readiness suites.
- New dedicated suite: 86 passed, 0 failed.
- Pre-existing failures at base (unchanged by this diff): 1 eslint error in
  `.github/`, duplicate test names in unrelated files, first-paint budget
  overage, web-suite `localStorage` environment failures.

## Net LOC

+2,017 / -0 across 9 files.

- New: `src/core/routing/task-bandit.ts` 782, `test/task-bandit.test.ts`
  623, `test/fixtures/task-bandit/history.jsonl` 227,
  `docs/router/task-bandit.md` 93, `test/fixtures/task-bandit/README.md`
  25, `BRIDGE_NOTES.md` (this file).
- Modified (all additive): `src/core/routing/policy.ts` +116,
  `src/core/routing/types.ts` +78, `src/core/routing/router.ts` +72,
  `docs/README.md` +1.

## Notes / limitations

- Flag is per-invocation: a caller supplies config, persisted posteriors,
  hints and pacing evidence via `RouteOptions.taskBandit`; dispatch today
  passes no `taskBandit`, so fleet routing is byte-identical. Wiring live
  state persistence is the natural follow-up and needs a storage decision.
- `model`/`effort` on an arm are advisory for downstream dispatch — the
  seat router admits a seat by engine, and `SeatBanditNote.divergent` is
  measured at engine granularity for that reason.
- Replay estimator is rejection sampling: it credits only records whose
  logged arm matches the draw, so it cannot estimate counterfactuals for
  arms the log never took; `held`/`unknownArmRecords` are reported, not
  imputed.
- No `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, release or publish config touched; nothing
  committed or pushed — all changes are uncommitted in this worktree.
</details>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-ONB-3-KEYS-CUSTODY

## Summary

API keys into Phantom Secrets custody, behind the local loopback console only.

- `src/core/onboard/catalog.ts`: `apiKeyCatalogResources()` selects catalog
  `apikey` rows that carry a vault env NAME and a validate endpoint (grok,
  openai, anthropic, google).
- `src/core/onboard.ts`: `custodyApiKey(resource, value)` validates the key
  shape BEFORE any spawn, pipes the value to `phantom add <KEY> --stdin` on
  stdin only (never argv, matching `storePatViaPhantom` in src/cli/pulse.ts),
  then runs exactly one cheap provider GET inside `phantom exec -- <node -e
  script>` where Phantom injects the stored secret. Child stdio is ignored;
  the child's whole contract is its exit code (0 accepted, 2 rejected,
  else unreachable -> validated: null). Callers get only
  `{resource, envName, masked: "****last4", stored, validated}`.
  `apiKeyCustodyStatus()` returns names-only stored flags from
  `getPhantomStatus().secretNames`.
- `src/core/readiness.ts`: `ReadinessPhantomSnapshot.apiKeyCustody
  {eligible, stored}` counted from catalog env names vs. secret NAMES; the
  phantom info detail now ends `api keys X/Y in custody`.
- `src/core/web/api.ts`: `GET /api/connect/keys` (names-only) and
  `POST /api/connect/key` behind the same loopback + x-ashlr-token +
  JSON content-type mutation gate as every write (codeless 404 without
  --allow-dispatch). The remote gateway deny-lists unlisted paths, so
  neither route can ever be reached via phm.dev.
- `src/web-ui`: `connectKeysQuery`, `connectApiKey()` mutation, and key
  forms in ConnectView for apikey rows only. Remote/gateway sessions
  (`isRemoteMobileMode()`) render an explanatory line instead of any
  input, and the status query is disabled so nothing is fetched remotely.
  Submitted values are never rendered; on success the field clears and the
  UI shows only the masked last-4 plus the verdict. The pending plaintext
  is dropped if the MutationTokenDialog is cancelled. CSS classes added.

The secret-shape gate (scrub-secrets) is untouched. No new outward network
primitive was added: the only network call runs inside the `phantom exec`
child, which is the established vault-execution boundary.

- `test/connect-key-custody.test.ts` (12 tests): spawn-routed phantom mock
  proves the value reaches Phantom ONLY as stdin to `add`, argv/env stay
  value-free, exactly one `exec` runs, pre-spawn gates reject before any

## Summary

Implemented an idempotent conflict-recut ingestion path on the merged-PR
router queue (`src/core/fleet/router-queue.ts`), the same proposal-only handoff
the trusted bridge already feeds with verified merge events.

- `enqueueRouterRecut(event)` accepts an independently verified
  `{v:1,state:'CONFLICTING',prUrl,headSha,baseRef,observedAt}` observation and
  queues one deterministic recut job keyed by `(prUrl, headSha)`:
  - replay of the same observation → `duplicate` (idempotent across retries,
    including after completion);
  - a moved source head supersedes the queued recut for the old one — never
    two live recuts for one PR;
  - a stale observation (a newer head, or a recorded merge) → `obsolete`;
  - a head that moves back revives its superseded receipt only when the new
    observation postdates every other one on record;
  - conflicting metadata (same head/different base, different heads at the
    same instant) fails closed.
- `enqueueRouterFollowup` now supersedes queued conflict recuts for the same
  PR when a merge lands — a merged source can never leave a live recut.
- `completeRouterJob` records `completedAt`; receipts gained `enqueuedAt`/
  `completedAt` timing (both-absent legacy rows still validate).
- `routerQueueStats()` measures queue health over the receipt log:
  outstanding/done/superseded totals, per-kind (merge vs recut) depth,
  oldest/mean outstanding queue age, mean/max event→completion latency,
  mean/max queue residence, and `latencyUnknown` for pre-timing receipts —
  no invented timing for legacy rows.

## Change

- Added the closed, versioned JSON Schema at `schema/handoff.v1.schema.json`.
- Added immutable typed `plan`, `delegate`, `ask`, `review`, `takeover`, and `result` messages in `src/core/fleet/handoff.ts`.
- Required fields: `version: 1`, `kind`, `taskId`, `fromProvider`, `toProvider`, and `payloadRefs`. Provider identifiers are extensible lowercase slugs. References use opaque `namespace:id` locators, with bounded lengths/counts and no duplicates.
- Added `parseHandoff`, `serializeHandoff`, and `deserializeHandoff`. Runtime admission rejects unknown fields, recognized credential values, unsafe object/array properties, and oversized wire input. Errors never include submitted content.
- Added the typed `handoff` fleet event. Direct emissions are validated and copied into a deeply frozen snapshot before subscribers run. Invalid messages are dropped under the existing never-throws bus contract. Existing flag-off and handler failure behavior remain intact.
- Added 58 tests covering schema validation, all six kinds, wire/bus round trips, boundaries, secret-field/value rejection, object inspection defenses, immutable delivery, flag-off, handler failure, and unsubscribe.

Billing class is a routing fact: subscription, metered, local, and loopback producers stay off merge and credential roles. The model table is the 2026-10-25 Mac inventory. Ollama remains the fallback. Local and loopback backends still cannot merge or hold a credential role. ## Real - Catalog, env allowlist, availability probe, and a separate model exec probe. - Rate-limit cooldown. A limit with no reset stays cooled. - `phm worker --dry-run` and `phm worker plan` print a plan and spawn nothing. - Pinned `route:codex`, `route:claude`, and `route:grok`. Grok stays out until `--enable-metered`. A status line that reports a subscription login is classified ahead of the `XAI_API_KEY` line. - `executeStep` builds `git worktree` and `gh pr create --draft` through an injected runner. The env is scrubbed. - Merge authority refuses a proposal that carries `billingClass`. Untagged historical frontier proposals keep the existing gate. - Devin's key is read only from `process.env.DEVIN_API_KEY`. The catalog secret name and `SecretLookup.get` are not consulted. The key is absent from the plan, the command list, the result detail, and logs. - oMLX probe is `GET /v1/models` on a loopback base URL, with no API key. A remote URL is refused and is not requested. ## Stubbed - `phm worker drain` exits 2. - `route:any` selection, the classifier, pool spend order, and the ledger are the following drafts. - Cursor, Devin session create, the oMLX edit loop, and the Ollama edit loop do not spawn here. - No named model is sent yet, because the inventory has no `accepted` row. body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-DOTFEED-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `ac173499c`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-DOTFEED-1

## Summary

Teammate iMessage findings → durable local agent bus. The comms poll already
receipts allowlisted non-Mason texts into `<runs>/imessage/teammates.jsonl`;
this change adds a best-effort mirror that posts each durable teammate row to
the local bus on the `teammate.findings` topic so fleet agents can observe and
claim findings (`ashlr fleet bus-claim acquire --id imessage-teammate-<rowid>`).

- One row → one envelope: deterministic id `imessage-teammate-<rowid>` (dedup
  by rowid — store-side exact-envelope dedupe makes every retry idempotent),
  `from`/sender = hashed `imessage:<sha256-16>` id, channel `imessage`,
  priority P2, 7-day TTL, strict v2 `{kind:'note', text, thread, refs}` body.
- Value-blind: no content classification or routing on content; reports carry
  counts and rowids only — never text or handles. Raw handles never reach the
  bus, logs or reports.
- Findings are untrusted data, never `kind:'work'` — the work loop cannot
  claim, select argv or execute them; claiming is local coordination only.
- Watermark `imessage/findings-bridge.json` (mode 0600, atomic private write)
  records the last handled rowid so expired envelopes are never reposted;
  corrupt state reports `unavailable`, never silently resets. Non-envelopable
  rows (empty/secret-shaped/oversize) count `refused` and are skipped
  permanently; transient store states stop the pass and leave rows `pending`.
- Loopback-only: reads one local JSONL + appends to the local bus store; no
  listener, no send path, no model, no authority. Passes serialize under
  `findings-bridge.lock` (contended → `busy`), batch-capped at 64 rows.
- Wired into `ingestIMessages` as a nonblocking tail stage: it runs after every
  post-gate return path (ingested/baselined/poll-error) so durable backlog
  drains even on empty or failed polls, and it never changes receipts, the
  intake cursor, or `ok`/`state`. Mason/operator texts keep `publish: null`
  and are never mirrored.

## Files

  locked watermark scan pass + `FindingsBridgeReport`.
- `src/core/comms/imessage-inbox-bridge.ts` — `busRoot`/`bridgeFindings` dep

  only when nonzero; JSON output carries the full report.
- `test/imessage-findings-bridge.test.ts` — new: 17 focused cases (envelope
  mapping, refusals, watermark, dedup, busy/pending, value-blind reports).

reconcilers already append — exposed via two `phm` status surfaces so the UI

  IO wrapper + `*Lines` output boundary re-validation + `sourceState`).
  Per job: newest stage (`queued|running|finished|published|merged|closed`),
  boundary ISO timestamps, `queueWaitS`/`runS`/`publishLagS`/`ageS` timings,
  dispatcher-reported `wallS`/`tokensTotal`/`exitCode`, allowlisted PR `url`,
  and a bounded (12-entry) structured `timeline` of lifecycle events — the
  event log half of the ask. Repeated job ids fold into the newest attempt
  (a queue/launch event newer than the terminal boundary resets; older
  stragglers never wipe a terminal attempt; stale outcomes cannot close a
  re-launched job). Bounded tail read: last 4 MiB / 3000 lines, 6 h window
  default (max 168 h), 50-job page (max 500). Job ids, lanes, repos, tiers,
  models, outcomes and URLs are all regex-allowlisted; malformed rows are
  counted in `dropped` and degrade `sourceState`, never throw.

title: fix(release-train): dispatch tag-ref builds with the App token
body:
## Why

Nothing has published since v3.30.24. Auto-tag creates a draft, but `ci.yml` has no `on.push.tags` trigger, so the tag itself never starts the desktop release-gate build. The train *does* dispatch `ci.yml` with `release_gate=true`, but today it:

1. Uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not the ashlr-release App token (only draft PATCH and enqueue used the App token).
2. Dispatches on `master` when `masterSha === tagSha`, so the run does not appear under `head_branch=v3.30.30` and does not use the `phantom-release-<tag>` concurrency group.

A train dispatch on master for v3.30.30 already ran as https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/actions/runs/42750808624 and failed later at the clean-tree gate (`docs/llms.txt`); that is a separate fix. This PR makes every new tag get an explicit App-token `workflow_dispatch` on the tag ref.

## Change

- `buildTrain` always uses `headTag.name` as the CI/attest dispatch ref, even when that commit is also master HEAD. npm publish stays on `master`.
- `gh()` sends workflow dispatches with `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`.
- Auto-tag, when it just created the draft (`release=draft-created`), dispatches `ci.yml` with `release_gate=true` on `v$VERSION` using the App token.
- Both workflows request `permission-actions: write` on the existing ashlr-release App token, still limited to this repository. No `pull_request_target`, no widening of `workflow_run` to run head code, no change to signing, notarization, attestation gates, required checks, tag peel, SHA equality, or KILL.

## Test

`npx vitest run test/release-train.test.ts` — 24 passed, including a new test that workflow dispatches use the App token and that an identical tag/master SHA still dispatches on the tag ref.

Security: the App token permission change is repo-scoped `actions: write` so the already-installed ashlr-release app can call `workflow_dispatch`. Please confirm the app installation allows that permission.

title: fix(release-train): drop buildCooldown, fixed waits, and the hourly enqueue floor
body:
## Why

Security agreed in advance to this scoped train fix. A green ancestor tag currently sits at `next=build` without a `ci.yml` dispatch because (1) `workflow_run` trains set `RELEASE_TRAIN_DISPATCH_BUILD=false` except after Auto-tag, (2) a 6-hour `buildCooldown` from a failed release-gate run on `2eba5f23` blocks retry until 1:35 AM ET, and (3) `cappedCadenceMinutes` raises any sub-hour cadence to 60 minutes before auto-enqueue.

## Change

- Remove `buildCooldown` / `failedBuildWithin` and dispatch a green candidate without the 6-hour wait.
- Remove the hosted 12-minute pending-CI poll (`settleCandidateCi`).
- Remove the `DISPATCH_BUILD=false` toggle on `workflow_run` trains so later CI completions can dispatch the tag build.
- Remove the 60-minute auto-enqueue floor in `cappedCadenceMinutes`. Valid cadence remains 1–1440 minutes. `.github/scripts/release-cadence.mjs` is untouched.
- Keep the existing train (`phantom-release-train`) and auto-tag (`auto-tag-${{ github.repository }}`) concurrency groups, both `cancel-in-progress: false`.
- Key release-gate CI concurrency on the tag/ref (`phantom-release-${{ github.ref_name }}`) and npm publish concurrency on the version (`phantom-canonical-npm-${{ inputs.version }}`), both `cancel-in-progress: false`.
- Re-run the strictly-greater tag check immediately before npm publish dispatch (and again on a fresh observation before applying that write) so a second train cannot publish when a newer tag has landed.

Required checks, tag peel, `GITHUB_SHA==CANDIDATE_SHA`, attestor==peeled tag sha, the strictly-greater version predicate itself, signing, notarization, attestation, the signer pin, and KILL are unchanged. No Mac signer files, no new permissions, no `pull_request_target`, and no widening of `workflow_run` to run head code with write tokens.

## Test

`npx vitest run test/release-train.test.ts` — 23 passed, including a double-train publish race.

  `imessage-outbox.ts` only sends text that a caller passes to it.

## Paths taken (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- <path>` from pull/4552/head)
- `src/core/comms/imessage-leader-replies.ts` (new)
- `src/cli/imessage.ts` (`phm imessage replies [--json]`; `poll --apply` runs the pass)

original `createdAt`/`updatedAt`/`lastTouchedAt`. Untagged JSON/JSONL keeps

`writeLedger`, so the batch fails atomically (verified: destination bytes
unchanged when the bad file is second in the batch). Secret-text checking is
unchanged — `writeLedger`'s `assertLedgerText` still scans the merged ledger.
No status is invented or lowered: `absorb`/`preferStatus` semantics apply as
before, and native items bypass `importStatus` because they already carry a
schema-valid status.

body:

# RQ-PHX-SLACKSTATUSANSWER42: Slack "Phantom status" gets a status reply in the same thread

## What changed
- `src/core/agents/owner-status-reply.ts` (new, 27 lines):
  - `isOwnerStatusRequest(text)` matches only exact short asks: status, phantom status, fleet status, /status, what's/whats the status. It trims, lowercases, strips trailing `?`/`.`/`!`, and returns false above 40 characters.
  - `composeOwnerStatusReply(runsDir, now, { brief? })` uses `leaderDailyBrief`. It swaps the "Morning leader brief" heading for `Phantom status, HH:MM ET` (24-hour clock, America/New_York) and caps the text at 1500 characters. On any throw it returns the fixed fallback text. It never throws.
- `src/core/agents/slack-leader.ts` (+21/-2):
  - When `network.ingest` returns `accepted` with a requestId and the routed text is a status ask, it calls `network.reply(requestId, …)`.
  - Compose is bounded at 10 s and falls back to the fixed text on timeout or rejection.
  - New optional `statusReply` seam on `SlackLeaderOptions`.
  - **Wiring fix:** the ingest-time `createLeaderNetwork` had no `deliver`, so `reply()` there could only draft. It now passes the existing `deliverSlackLeaderMessage`, the same function `flushSlackLeaderReplies` already uses. There is no second delivery path, and send policy, owner checks, `confirmedByMason` and the journal are unchanged.
  - **Detached reply:** `openSlackSocket` acks the Slack envelope only after `route` resolves. If the brief read and post were awaited inline, the ack would be held for up to 35 s, and Slack redelivers after about 3 s. So the reply runs as a detached promise, and its outcome never affects `{ owned, durable }`.
  - Duplicates (`status: 'duplicate'`) never reply. The inbox line is still written, so the ask stays visible in MASON-INBOX.md.
  - Note: the auto-answer owns the request's reply slot. `tickLeaderNetwork` will not generate a second model reply for that same "status" message (tested).
- `test/owner-status-reply.test.ts` (new): 12 true and 12 false matcher cases, the 40-character boundary, heading replacement (including across DST), the 1500-character cap, and the fallback text.
- `test/slack-leader-status-reply.test.ts` (new): drives `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope` through the real socket mapper with fake `U0FAKEOWNER` ids. It covers:
  - (a) exactly one same-thread `chat.postMessage` with `Leader: <status text>`, and the inbox still records the ask;
  - (b) a redelivered duplicate does not recompose or post, and a Leader tick generates nothing;
  - (c) "please fix the release" gets no auto reply;
  - (d) an unverified peer, a bot-backed owner id and a forged envelope get nothing;
  - plus: a status read failure posts the fallback, and a failed post keeps the ingest durable and acked.

`composeOwnerStatusReply` and `isOwnerStatusRequest` are channel-agnostic. The Telegram and iMessage owner routes can reuse them with the same 3-line hook after their own `network.ingest` returns `accepted`.

title: fix(release-train): do not treat pending or later check suites as red
body:
## Why

The release train is stopping on `candidate-ci-red` while trying to publish the newest release-please tag, `v3.30.29` (`2eba5f23`). That commit is an ancestor of master and already has a successful required `Merge Gate`. The train then sees later `Merge Gate` rows from other check suites (tag or push CI) whose job fails outside the merge queue, and `judgeRequiredChecks` treats any non-success match as red.

The workflow run head is current master (`9189dc3d`, the #4582 bridge merge). That is not the candidate SHA, and there is still no `v3.30.30` tag. Dispatching the train again on master would select the same poisoned tag; dispatching on the tag ref would also run pre-#4577 train code. This PR is the forward fix.

## Change

- Judge only the named required checks (today, `Merge Gate`).
- Ignore the release-train job (`train`) even if it appears in the required list, so a failed train retry cannot poison the same SHA.
- If a required context already has a successful run, a later failed or skipped suite of the same name does not turn the candidate red.
- Queued or in-progress required checks are `pending`, not red.
- On `--apply`, recheck pending required CI for up to 12 minutes (30s interval) before planning writes.

Unit tests cover the later-suite case, ignored `train` failures, pending vs red, and the bounded poll.

## Test

`npx vitest run test/release-train.test.ts` — 23 passed.
